findings.title: `queued` default is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` makes the default value a single `datetime` computed when the module is first imported, not when an `AssignmentSource` is created. Every instance built via `from_integration()` (or any constructor call that omits `queued`) will therefore carry the process-start timestamp, so the field is useless for measuring how long the assignment context has been in flight and will look increasingly stale in long-running workers. Use `dataclasses.field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: from_dict does no validation and silently drops the cycle-protection context
findings.body: `from_dict` constructs the dataclass with `cls(**input_dict)` and returns `None` on any `TypeError`/`ValueError`. Two problems: (1) failures are silent — if the payload shape ever changes (e.g. a field is renamed or an extra key is added by a producer on a different deploy), the loop-prevention context is dropped with no log/metric and the sync cycle this PR is meant to fix reappears; (2) no type coercion is done, so after the dict round-trips through the celery broker the `queued` value comes back as an ISO string, not a `datetime`, violating the field's annotation for any future consumer that does date arithmetic on it. Consider logging when parsing fails and explicitly parsing `queued`.

findings.title: New task kwarg breaks mixed-version workers during rollout
findings.body: `sync_assignee_outbound` is an `@instrumented_task` whose signature now accepts `assignment_source_dict`, and `sync_group_assignee_outbound` always includes that key in `apply_async(kwargs=...)`. During a rolling deploy, tasks enqueued by new web/region code can be picked up by workers still running the old signature, which will raise `TypeError: sync_assignee_outbound() got an unexpected keyword argument 'assignment_source_dict'` and burn the task's retries, dropping assignee syncs for those messages. Only send the new kwarg when it is non-None, or guard the task with `**kwargs`.

findings.title: `assignment_source` added to sync_status_outbound but never used or implemented
findings.body: The abstract `sync_status_outbound` now declares a 4th parameter `assignment_source`, but no caller passes it and no concrete integration implementation was updated to accept it (they rely on `**kwargs`). The result is a parameter in the published ABC signature that is dead code, misleadingly named for a status (not assignment) sync, and implies status-sync cycles are also guarded when they are not. Either wire it through the status-sync path (task + implementations) or drop it from this PR.

findings.title: New `assignment_source` kwarg forwarded to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`, but no concrete integration implementation was updated in this PR. Any provider implementation of `sync_assignee_outbound` that does not declare `**kwargs` (or an explicit `assignment_source` parameter) will raise `TypeError` at runtime for every outbound assignee sync. Please confirm every implementation (Jira, Jira Server, VSTS, and any third-party/plugin installation returning `should_sync`) tolerates the extra keyword, or pass it only when it is not None.

findings.title: No test that a different source integration still propagates outbound
findings.body: The added coverage only asserts the suppression case (`AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` matching the target integration blocks the outbound call). There is no test that an assignment originating from a *different* integration still produces an outbound sync, which is the main over-blocking regression risk of the new `should_sync` short-circuit, nor a test covering the celery boundary (`assignment_source_dict` serialized in `sync_group_assignee_outbound` and re-parsed in the task). Add a case with a second integration whose id differs, and a case asserting the dict round-trip yields a usable `AssignmentSource`.
